system.summary: Mayenne-Forget's Cipher-2 (Tomokiyo's reconstruction): homophonic substitution of invented signs and figures for French letters, with signs for syllables and common words (de, la, que, qui, est, et, pour, plus, monsieur, 23 apres, 24 peu, 31 pas, 17 tant) and a slash as word divider.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's reconstruction of Mayenne-Forget's Cipher-2 (cryptiana henryiii_MayenneForget2.png), with values Burford aligned on letters in the same cipher deciphered at the time: fr. 15573 ff. 103v-104r (Mayenne to the King, Libourne, Sept 1586), 7v-8r, 32r-33r, 97r, 149r-150r.
system.notes: One key across the three documents: ff. 218-219 were read with Tomokiyo's table (Harumi-Matsuba checked ten values against Burford's key after the fact), f. 120 with Burford's key, f. 385 is Burford's own. Not Cipher-1 (matignon1586) or Cipher-3 (matignon1586c3): different sign inventory (barred # signs, ∴, // dividers). Code numbers do not carry across the three ciphers. Two sign readings conflict between the contributors: barred h is armée in Harumi's key, while Burford splits it into hb = tout and Qh = armée; the χ° sign is q in the table but pour in the calibration letter.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana henryiii.htm (2023): the Cipher-2 table; for f. 385 a fragment of the opening credited to George Lasry. No reading of ff. 218-219 or f. 120 found by the contributors (searches of 19-20 Oct 2026; DECODE and Lasry's publications not checked by Harumi-Matsuba).

solution.what: When matignon1586 was split, catalogue item 12 was narrowed to the Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219, not viewed or attempted here; the 'Cipher-2' values once read off f. 79r had been withdrawn (f. 79r is Cipher-1).

Contributed (Brett Burford, issue #46, v0.1-v0.2): fr. 15573 f. 385r-v, 2,052 signs named by Claude Opus 5.5 in five voted passes; Tomokiyo's Cipher-2 key checked on ff. 103v-104r against their contemporary decipherment, code values aligned on five more deciphered letters (ff. 7v-8r, 32r-33r, 97r, 149r-150r); his measure 0.921 / 0.929 per page, shuffled 0.59-0.62; 12 code signs and 36 short stretches open.

Contributed (Harumi-Matsuba, issue #49, v0.1): fr. 15572 ff. 218-219, 2,139 signs transcribed by Claude in one pass with Tomokiyo's table; values inferred in the letter (27 = d, 17 = tant, barred h = armée, yy = encore ...); calibration on f. 103v ll. 1-6: 74.8% letter agreement; independent Codex transcription 72-86% value agreement.

Contributed (Harumi-Matsuba, issue #51): fr. 15573 f. 120r-v (not in the ledger), 1,103 signs, Burford's key plus three inferred values (ooo = escus, struck gg = nous, curled stroke = o); Codex second transcription 92.2% / 89.9%; calibration f. 104r 90.5% per sign. No person checked it.

Review here: views 225-226 of fr. 15572 (f. 218v 34 cipher lines, f. 219r 19 lines, clear closing 'Du camp devant Monsegur ... May 1586' signed Matignon), view 246 of fr. 15573 (f. 120r, 31 lines wholly in cipher, a few small superscript marks) and view 752 (f. 385r, 34 lines) checked against the contributors' line counts and descriptions; same sign inventory on all three. Issues reviewed for one-key-per-entry: all three documents use Cipher-2 and form this one entry.

Re-measured with the matignon1586c3 rule (f276/scripts/measure.py, fr-1600-letters, 20 shuffled keys) after to_read.py: f. 385r 851/1,054, 385v 851/998; f. 218r 611/713, 218v 790/926, 219r 454/499; f. 120r 814/885, 120v 188/218; per document with pages joined 1,856 + 1,002 + 1,702 = 4,560 of 5,293 tokens (86.1%); shuffled medians 9.5-15.9%, max 36%. The measure counts sense, not correctness: on known text the transcriptions were 75-93% right.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the contributors' own files linked: Harumi-Matsuba's sign transcriptions, mechanical decodes and READING.en.md for ff. 218-219 and f. 120; Brett Burford's signs.txt, plaintext-by-line, French and English text for f. 385; their keys as key_file.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): ff. 218-219 read (A); f. 120 has holes in most sentences of several paragraphs, and f. 385 is a self-declared partial unspaced decode (both C confirmed). Both relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part kept; fraction_read 0.861 -> 0.404.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b21), f. 120 and f. 385. Step 1: no DECODE record; Gallica btv1b90618780 views 244-249 and 750-755 fetched (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF). f. 119r-v is a clear memorandum on Navarre, Biron and Champigny, not a decipherment; f. 121r blank, f. 121v the cover of the f. 120 letter, addressed 'Pour Monseigneur de Villeroy', docket '1586'. Around f. 385: an address leaf 'Au Roy' (view 751, letter not established) and blank leaves; no decipherment, interlinear or separate, and no clear copy for either letter. The superscripts on f. 120r are cipher signs (writer's insertions), not glosses.

f. 120r at full resolution (view 246) cut into line strips; checked r c01 (opening thb + 7 I Sbar as transcribed, no value), c11 (superscript 'ar' = two cipher signs), c30 ('sort' as transcribed), c31: the sign read curlo before 'inances' has the shape of the delta (e) later in the line, so 'finances' rests on a look-alike alternate. Other lines not re-read.

f. 120: Harumi-Matsuba's reading checked word by word against his decode (b21_may_check.py: 302 of 326 plain words carried letter for letter, the rest two-valued-sign choices or letters the reading had added); the figures' spelling restored where the reading had normalised (enuyé, soufre, efects, somes, pouoir, ...), added letters bracketed, partly carried words written [?word] (f120_harumi/f120_reading.md). Checker 0.50 (17/34), explicit holes 0.647 (22/34); before 0.50 / 0.625. The sentences of r c15-c19, c24-c31 and v c03-c05 do not hold: kept decoded, not read.

f. 385: Burford's literal v0.2 decode divided into words and punctuated, letters unchanged (f385_burford/f385_reading.md; b21_may_check.py 450 of 453 plain words carried). Checker 0.222 (10/45), explicit holes 0.244 (before: f385-french.md 0.233). Only f. 385v ll. 1-8, 18-21 hold: kept decoded, not read; the v0.2 unread stretches need a sign-by-sign image round.

Consistency pass (cl): 'read in part' not justified because ff. 120 and 385 still need the sign-by-sign re-read named in their gap lines (not-attempted kept; NOTES already Status: in progress). The f. 120 gap line carried a second blocker in its text; moved to the code-signs line. outcome.gaps mirrors the list.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): f. 120 r c15-c19, c24-c31, v c03-c05 re-read sign by sign on Gallica views 246-247 (full resolution), transcription frozen by SHA-256 before decoding: 8 signs changed (w -> w2 'il m'est', 9 -> q+ 'spe[ci]alement', ls -> S 'au ser[v]ice', B -> 6b, two v-with-bar signs, an 8-shaped g), 13 doubtful signs listed. One pre-registered measure on the 16 lines (453 tokens, key unchanged): 0.903 vs 0.909 for the earlier transcription, every one of 400 controls below (permuted keys max 0.428, shuffled text max 0.695): the second pre-registered criterion (re-read >= earlier transcription) FAILED, the corrections rest on the sign forms and not on a score. Reading counted with the 95% rule: 88.3% -> 90.0% of letters sure or probable (89.4% sure only; both under 95%) (dudout/README.md). Integration check 12 Nov 2026: measure and counts reproduced; line r28 spot-checked on the Gallica image.

texts.label: fr. 15572 ff. 218r-219r, Matignon to Henri III, camp before Monségur, May 1586 (Harumi-Matsuba)
texts.summary: Matignon reports the battery before Monségur: about twelve hundred shots with less effect than hoped, three breaches, Sacramore de Birague badly wounded trying for the lodgement. The army is in need, the forces shrink daily and the pay is what matters most; Mayenne has a fever, but the physicians see no danger.
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 92.2% of the words of f218_219_harumi/f218_219_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: fr. 15573 f. 120r-v, autumn 1586, sender and recipient unknown (Harumi-Matsuba)
texts.summary: "This prince" is more vexed than ever; the treasurer Bilart wrote that thirty thousand écus in gold have been ready for ten days, the Cardinal of Guise writes that five thousand are coming, but not even a hundred and five thousand would set the army right. Biron cannot be kept; deputies of the army have come; papers of the secretary La Marsilière have fallen into "our" hands.

texts.label: fr. 15573 f. 385r-v, from Mayenne's side, autumn 1586 (Brett Burford, v0.2)
texts.summary: The army in Guyenne is breaking up at the start of winter 1586: not a thousand foot left, men asking for leave, no powder. The letter asks what to do with the regiments and the foreigners over the winter, and names the landsknechts from Champagne, a company of light horse, Monsieur d'Halincourt, Monsieur de Matignon and La Roche.
